surfaces.part: top cap / header of the sign board
sign board front face with the white 카페 lettering

answer.evidence: The tall board is a vertical front face (rows 6-29) with white Hangul lettering. At the top, rows 1-4 form a separate cap band. Its silhouette is narrower at the top (width 9, then 11, then 13), and its lighter brown rows 1-3 sit over a darker row 4 and the near-black outline at row 5. That darker row and outline act as a front-edge line and eave shadow, so the cap reads as a small top surface about 4 rows tall. It could also be read as a face-on header strip, so this call is only moderately confident. No receding side face is drawn, and the bottom strip at rows 29-30 is a base.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin vertical sign: a brown slab with a lighter cap and a lit left edge, a darker right edge, a tinted dark-brown edge, and cream hangul glyphs. The glyphs break up the face, so no large flat areas remain. The measured facts back this up: 7 visible tones per tile, against 6 for bus-shelter-a, 12 for kiosk-a and 20 for vending-a. Near-flat coverage is 7%, against 9% for the bus shelter. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a brown tint rather than a black sticker line. By eye, the body ramp is shallower than the kiosk and vending machine (about 4 steps against 5-6) and its grain is sparse. That is expected for a plain sign, and it sits at the level of the accepted bus-shelter reference. It would not look thinner or more sticker-like beside the shelter.

surfaces.part: sign board face with Korean lettering

answer.evidence: The top cap spans rows 1-4. It has a lighter highlight on row 1 and mid-brown on rows 2-3, and the silhouette widens from 9 to 11 to 13 px from row 0 to row 3, which gives a trapezoid top plane. A darker front-edge line sits on row 4, followed by the dark outline and eave shadow on row 5. Below it the vertical board face runs rows 6-28 with the white lettering, and a base strip fills rows 29-30, so the front face is about 25 rows. No side face is drawn. The cap is only 4 rows and is borderline against a front-facing cornice strip, but the width taper and the edge line with shadow support a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall brown sign board with white Korean text '카페'. It has a darker brown edge, a lighter left highlight strip, and a mid-brown body, so about 4 lightness steps on the main ramp. The bus-shelter reference has a similar number of steps (6 tones), but kiosk-a (12 tones) and vending-a (20 tones) are richer. Measured facts: 7 visible tones per tile is within the range of bus-shelter (6) but well below kiosk (12) and vending (20). Near-flat coverage is 7%, comparable to bus-shelter (9%) and above the 0% of the richer references. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown rather than near-black. The sign face is mostly a uniform mid-brown with only a light edge strip and the lettering, so there is little grain or variation. It is acceptable as a simple sign, matches the simplest shipped reference, and is not a sticker-style piece, but it is thinner than the kiosk and vending references.

surfaces.part: top cap of the sign (lighter beveled band)
main signboard front face with text

answer.evidence: The top has a 4-row cap in rows 1-4. The silhouette widens from 9 to 11 to 13 px, rows 1-3 have a pink highlight band, and row 4 is a darker line. Row 5 is a dark edge line that acts as a shadow before the board face. Below it the board front runs from row 6 to about row 29 with the white text, plus a grey base strip at row 30. The cap is only weakly a top surface, since it could also be read as a header strip, but the highlight band, the dark edge line and the narrowing of the silhouette at the top are enough for evidence (a). The front face is much taller than 3 rows.

surfaces.part: top cap of the sign board

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall board with a lighter, narrower top cap in rows 1-3 (widths 9, 11, 11, then 13 from row 3). Row 4 is a darker line and row 5 is a dark outline row, which together act as the edge line and shadow. The front face is rows 6-30 (brown board with white lettering and a gray base at rows 29-30). No side face is drawn. The top is thin (about 3 rows), and a header-strip reading is possible, but the lighter band followed by an edge line and shadow qualifies as a top surface under (a).
